sentences.text: By means of the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.107 of 2023 at Police Station-Babina, District-Jhansi under Sections 363, 376 IPC and Sections 3/4 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in jail since 15.06.2023.

sentences.text: The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 21.08.2023.

The following arguments made by Shri Mahesh Kumar, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant,
which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Ms. Manisha Chaturvedi, learned counsel for the opposite party/victim and Shri Paritosh Kumar Malviya, learned AGA-I from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The victim was wrongly shown as a minor of 14 years in the F.I.R. only to falsely implicate the applicant under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act and cause his imprisonment.
2.The age of the victim set out in the prosecution case is refuted in light of the judgement of this Court in Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021) and on the following grounds:
(i) There are material contradictions in the age of the victim as recorded in various prosecution documents.
(ii) The victim in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has stated that she is 14 years of age.

entities.text: Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iii) Medico-legal examination (not the age determination test) records that the victim is about 13 years of age.
(iv). The medical report drawn up to determine the age of the victim opines that she is 14-15 years of age.
Two submissions are made in regard to the aforesaid medical report.
Firstly, the range of error in determining the age is about two years and the same should be read in favour of the applicant at this stage.
Secondly, the relevant scientific parameters as per latest medical protocol which would establish the majority of the victim has been excluded from consideration in the medical report.
For example, size of the teeth, heredity, socioeconomic environment and dietary habits have not been factored in the said medical reports.
These have a bearing on the human growth and determination of age.
The medical report is flawed.
In fact the victim is a major.

3. The incident occurred on 10.04.2023 and the F.I.R. was got registered on 11.04.2023.
4. Delay of one day in lodgement of the F.I.R. in the facts of this case is fatal to the prosecution case.
5. The victim and the applicant were intimate.
6. The F.I.R. is the result of opposition of the victim's family to the said relationship with the applicant.

sentences.text: 7. The victim in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has admitted to intimacy with the applicant.
The victim has further asserted that she eloped with the applicant and resided with him at Delhi of her own volition.
She has categorically asserted that she had consensual physical relations with the applicant.

8. The applicant has not made any allegation of commission of rape, abduction or forceful assault in the aforesaid statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
9.
False and aggravated allegations were made by the victim against the applicant in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. at the behest of her parents only to save the failing prosecution case.
However, in the aforesaid statement as well, the victim has admitted that she accompanied the applicant to New Delhi, though she claims that she had been intoxicated.
10. No intoxication has been depicted in the medical report.
11. The victim was never confined or bound down in any manner.
The victim was present at public places.
She did not raise an alarm nor did she resist the applicant.
Her conduct shows that she was a consenting party.
12. Major inconsistencies in the statements of the victim under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and Section 164 Cr.P.C., as well as the recitals in the F.I.R. discredit the prosecution case.
13. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
14. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from the instant case.
15. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Sanju Kewat be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.
The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
( i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
